marker: # ref_size is the product length measured in the Ames Ancestor assembly GCA_000008445.1 by in
# silico PCR with these primers, outer primer edge to outer primer edge. Every locus gives
# exactly one product, all are searchable at word size 11 and none needs the rescue pass. Each
# product lies on the replicon the publication states: the eleven chromosomal loci on
# AE017334.2, pXO1-aat on pXO1 (AE017336.2) and BaVNTR16, BaVNTR17 and pXO2-at on pXO2
# The publication's locations are coordinates in the A2012 numbering (NC_003995 for the
# chromosome, NC_003980 for pXO1, NC_003981 for pXO2), not in Ames Ancestor, so they were
# compared by span length rather than by position. All eight MLVA-8 loci reproduce their
# published span exactly: vrrA 314, vrrB1 229, CG3 158, pXO1-aat 126, pXO2-at 141, vrrB2 153,
# vrrC1 580 and vrrC2 532 bp.
# A non-genomic base in the new reverse primers. Each of the seven BaVNTR reverse primers
# begins with a 5' G that the genome does not carry; six of them therefore report one primer
# mismatch, and in BaVNTR19 the G happens to match. The primers are kept as published, because
# a real reaction with them yields a product one base longer than the genomic span, which is
# what ref_size records. Taking that one base into account, six of the seven loci agree with
# the published span: BaVNTR12, BaVNTR35, BaVNTR16 and BaVNTR17 match it when the extra base
# is excluded (114, 114, 272, 385 bp), and BaVNTR23 and BaVNTR32 match it when the extra base
# is included (197 and 577 bp), so the publication appears not to be consistent about whether
# the base is counted. BaVNTR19 is the exception: 96 bp here against a published span of 124,
# and a difference of 28 bp is not a whole number of TAT units, so it is not a simple allele
# difference. It is either a strain difference between A2012 and Ames Ancestor combined with
# an indel, or a coordinate error; it could not be settled without the A2012 sequence.
# unit_length and patterns of the seven new loci are the repeat motifs the publication gives,
# except BaVNTR32, whose motif is stated only as Complex: the reference holds a clean 21 bp
# array there, GAAGAAACAGAAAAGCCAGGT, and the unit length is derived from it. The motifs given
# for the MLVA-8 loci corroborate the units in bacillus_mlva8_keim_2000: vrrA CAATATCAACAA is
# the stored pattern exactly, CG3 TAATA is the published rotation of the same 5 bp unit and is
# used here, pXO1-aat AAT and pXO2-at AT match, vrrB1 is described as a 9 bp degenerate repeat
# and vrrB2, vrrC1 and vrrC2 as Complex, which is what the reference shows.
# THE COPY NUMBERS ARE NOT PUBLISHED VALUES. The source table gives motifs, locations and
# primers but no allele definitions, so ref_repeats is the count the tandem array counter
# returns for the stored motif at the default mismatch allowance. MLVA-15 alleles are
# canonically assigned from fragment size against the published allele table, so a count here
# may be offset from the canonical allele by a constant. Confirm them against that table, or
# supply it as bins.tsv, before a profile from this scheme is compared with published MLVA-15
# genotypes. The twelve loci with a stored pattern carry an active repeat count cross-check
# that check-scheme reproduces; vrrC1 and vrrC2 do not, for the reason given in
# bacillus_mlva8_keim_2000, from which the eight shared loci take their values unchanged.
# BaVNTR32 holds about 14 units of its 21 bp motif in the reference, of which 11 are counted:
# the three outermost differ from the core by 5 to 8 of 21 bases and fall outside the default
# allowance. vrrB1 with vrrB2 and vrrC1 with vrrC2 are adjacent paralogues whose amplicons
# overlap by 27 and 36 bp, so a rearrangement there can move both members of a pair.
